clinicalVerdict: DEFECTIVE on option C, on two independent grounds both verified against primary sources. (1) No healthcare proxy exists: a healthcare proxy is named only by a durable power of attorney for health care, an instrument distinct from a living will, so completing 'the advance directive' with a daughter present does not appoint her; baseline affirmatively negates any HCPOA. (2) Even reframed as family notification, the patient is present and retains full decision-making capacity at 1130 (baseline documents full capacity; he speaks for himself at 1100 in stage_3). Under 45 CFR 164.510(b)(2) disclosure to a family member in that situation is permitted only where the entity obtains the individual's agreement, provides an opportunity to object with no objection expressed, or reasonably infers no objection by professional judgment. The 164.510(b)(3) best-interest pathway applies only when the individual is absent or incapacitated and is unavailable here. Keying C as an unconditional nursing action teaches an incorrect disclosure rule. Separately, proxy authority activates only on incapacity, so a capacitated patient has no operative proxy to notify.
contentDefects: PRIMARY: option C 'Notifying the healthcare proxy' hypothesises a decision-maker the chart never establishes and, as written, asserts an unconditional disclosure that 45 CFR 164.510(b)(2) does not permit for a present, capacitated patient.

The stem asks which actions 'evaluate the effectiveness of the advocacy process'; filing an incident report is a downstream reporting/QI action rather than an evaluation. Defensible under the evaluate_outcomes skill because identifying the system gap is itself evaluative, so I do not require removal, but if the item is reopened the stem could be widened to 'evaluate and follow up on' to remove the mismatch.
